topics.display_title: The Government of India Act 1935 & the Congress Ministries (1937–1939)

panels.title: Constitutional lineage, Simon to royal assent
ascii_lines: SIMON REPORT (1930) -> RTCs (1930-32) -> WHITE PAPER (1933)
-> JOINT SELECT COMMITTEE (1934) -> ROYAL ASSENT (1935)
INPUTS -> commission evidence + constitutional negotiation + parliamentary review
RULE -> five ordered stages; none may be skipped or reordered.
source_references: Constitutional lineage: from Simon to royal assent

panels.title: Two halves of the Act, federation never in force
ascii_lines: FEDERAL HALF -> All-India Federation + central dyarchy -> NEVER IN FORCE
PROVINCIAL HALF -> provincial autonomy, dyarchy abolished -> OPERATED 1937
ACCESSION FAILURE -> princely threshold remained unmet
RULE -> the federation's non-operation must never be blurred with the record.
source_references: Two halves of the Act and the federation that never operated

panels.title: Dyarchy: abolished provincially, unrealised centrally
ascii_lines: 1919 ACT -> provincial dyarchy (reserved + transferred subjects)
1935 ACT -> provincial dyarchy ABOLISHED -> provincial autonomy begins
PROVINCIAL MINISTERS -> responsible for all provincial subjects and departments
CENTRAL DYARCHY -> proposed only for the federal centre -> never operated.
source_references: Provincial dyarchy abolished, not merely modified

panels.title: Governor's powers versus Section 93
ascii_lines: DISCRETIONARY / SPECIAL RESPONSIBILITY -> continuous standing power
SECTION 93 -> emergency takeover only on breakdown of machinery
NORMAL AUTONOMY -> ministers govern while reserve powers remain in the background
1939 RESIGNATION -> caused by war declaration, not Section 93 action.
source_references: Governor's discretionary powers and special responsibilities
Section 93: the background emergency reserve power

panels.title: Reserved subjects and residuary power
ascii_lines: RESERVED TO GOVERNOR-GENERAL
|-- Defence
|-- External Affairs
|-- Ecclesiastical Affairs
`-- Tribal Areas
RESIDUARY POWER -> also with the Governor-General, not any legislature.
source_references: Reserved central subjects and residuary power

panels.title: Franchise reform as a qualified range
ascii_lines: ELECTORATE -> roughly 30 to 35 million voters (source-dependent)
SHARE OF POPULATION -> roughly 10 to 14 per cent (denominator-dependent)
QUALIFICATIONS -> property, tax, income and education restrictions remained
RULE -> state as a qualified range; still short of universal adult franchise.
source_references: Franchise reform as a qualified range, not one exact figure

panels.title: RBI Act 1934 versus the 1935 Act
ascii_lines: 1934 -> Reserve Bank of India Act -> RBI founded
1935 -> Government of India Act -> separate constitutional statute
1937 -> provincial constitutional provisions begin operating
TRAP -> RBI's origin is the 1934 Act, never the 1935 Act.
source_references: RBI Act 1934 versus the Government of India Act 1935

panels.title: Federal Court and Burma: parallel 1937 tracks
ascii_lines: 1935 ACT PROVISIONS -> two parallel 1937 developments
FEDERAL COURT OF INDIA -> begins functioning, 1937
BURMA SEPARATION -> takes effect, 1937
RULE -> parallel, not sequential or causally connected.
source_references: Federal Court and Burma separation: parallel 1937 developments

panels.title: 1937 election and ministry timing, NWFP and Assam
ascii_lines: FEB 1937 -> elections; Congress largest in most provinces
JUL 1937 -> six ministries: Madras, Bombay, UP, Bihar, CP and Orissa
LATER 1937 -> NWFP becomes the seventh Congress ministry
1938 -> Assam becomes the eighth after coalition arrangements break down
RULE -> eight is the eventual, not the simultaneous, total.
source_references: 1937 elections, ministry timing, NWFP and Assam

panels.title: Office-acceptance debate
ascii_lines: FOR -> reformist and organisational opportunity within autonomy
AGAINST -> risk of legitimising a rejected constitutional structure
SAFEGUARD TEST -> Congress sought assurances against routine governor interference
OUTCOME -> conditional acceptance, watching for governor interference.
source_references: The 1937 office-acceptance debate inside Congress

panels.title: Ministries' achievements and structural limits
ascii_lines: ACHIEVEMENTS -> civil liberties, prisoner release, tenancy/debt reform
ACHIEVEMENTS -> prohibition, primary education
LIMITS -> restricted finance, landlord legislatures, governor reserve powers
RESULT -> real gains; labour unrest and agrarian distress not fully resolved.
source_references: Achievements and structural limits of the Congress ministries

panels.title: 1939 resignation to Lahore, and the PYQ anchors
ascii_lines: OCT-NOV 1939 -> ministries resign (unconsulted war declaration)
22 DEC 1939 -> League Deliverance Day
MAR 1940 -> Lahore Resolution -> one link in a chain, not sole cause
PYQ -> 2024 Q62 key confirmed; 2018 Q38 source-backed, no key held.
source_references: 1939 resignation and the League's Deliverance Day
Lahore Resolution as one link, not the whole causal chain
PYQ anchors: confirmed 2024 key and cautious 2018 residuary recall

topics.display_title: Second World War, the Cripps Mission & Quit India (1939–1942)

panels.title: Unconsulted belligerency and the response chain
ascii_lines: 3 SEP 1939 -> Viceroy declares India a belligerent, no consultation
OCT-NOV 1939 -> Congress ministries resign
22 DEC 1939 -> League Deliverance Day -> MAR 1940 -> Lahore Resolution
RULE -> three connected but separately dated stages.
source_references: Unconsulted belligerency: 3 September 1939
Resignation to the Lahore Resolution: the connected chain

panels.title: August Offer: promise and minority-consent veto
ascii_lines: 8 AUG 1940 -> AUGUST OFFER
PROMISE -> expanded, representative post-war constitution-making body
CONDITION -> no constitution without minority consent (effective veto)
LIMIT -> no immediate national government offered.
source_references: August Offer, 1940: promise and its minority-consent veto

panels.title: Individual Satyagraha: sequence and limited objective
ascii_lines: 17 OCT 1940 -> Vinoba Bhave, first satyagrahi
NEXT -> Jawaharlal Nehru, second satyagrahi
METHOD -> selected individuals publicly assert the right to oppose the war
OBJECTIVE -> limited anti-war free-speech right, not mass civil disobedience.
source_references: Individual Satyagraha: sequence and its limited objective

panels.title: Cripps arrival and the March 1942 proposals
ascii_lines: MAR 1942 -> Cripps arrives in India
LATE MAR 1942 -> proposals announced
OFFER -> Dominion status after the war + post-war constitution-making body
LIMIT -> no change to India's status during the war itself.
source_references: Cripps Mission: arrival and the March 1942 proposals

panels.title: Cripps scheme: opt-out and princely nomination
ascii_lines: OPT-OUT -> any province or princely state may not join the new union
PRINCELY SEATS -> members nominated by rulers, not popularly elected
UNION DESIGN -> accession would be negotiated after the war
EFFECT -> both features fuelled objections from different political groups.
source_references: Cripps scheme: opt-out clause and ruler-nominated princely seats

panels.title: British wartime control and no immediate cabinet
ascii_lines: DEFENCE + WAR CONDUCT -> remain under British control throughout the war
NATIONAL CABINET -> none created immediately
EXECUTIVE GAP -> Indian leaders receive no present control over the wartime state
RULE -> a separate objection from the opt-out and princely-nomination features.
source_references: British wartime control and the absence of an immediate cabinet

panels.title: Multi-party rejection of the Cripps proposals
ascii_lines: CONGRESS -> deferred, conditional offer; no immediate responsible government
LEAGUE -> no guarantee of a separate Pakistan
SIKH / HINDU MAHASABHA -> separate minority and communal objections
PRINCELY OPINION -> concerns over opt-out and accession arrangements.
source_references: Multi-party rejection: different groups, different reasons

panels.title: Post-dated cheque phrase, cautious provenance
ascii_lines: SHORT PHRASE -> "post-dated cheque" -> well attested, safe to use
LONGER VERSION -> adds a crashing bank -> provenance uncertain
REFERENCE -> the criticism concerns deferred Cripps promises
RULE -> applies to Cripps only, never to the 1940 August Offer.
source_references: The 'post-dated cheque' phrase and its cautious use

panels.title: Quit India's two-stage resolution
ascii_lines: 14 JUL 1942, WARDHA -> Congress Working Committee approves resolution
8 AUG 1942, BOMBAY -> All-India Congress Committee ratifies resolution
POLITICAL MOVE -> committee draft becomes the national organisation's mandate
RULE -> two distinct bodies and dates; never a single date.
source_references: Quit India's two-stage resolution: Wardha then Bombay

panels.title: Operation Zero Hour, the following morning after Bombay
ascii_lines: 8 AUG 1942 -> AICC ratifies Quit India resolution at Bombay
9 AUG 1942 (early hours) -> Operation Zero Hour: mass arrests begin
CONSEQUENCE -> central leadership is removed before an organised campaign develops
RULE -> within hours, on the following calendar day; not a full 24-hour gap.
source_references: Operation Zero Hour: arrests the following morning

panels.title: Do or Die, Gowalia Tank and underground resistance
ascii_lines: 8 AUG 1942 -> Gandhi's "Do or Die" call, before his arrest
GOWALIA TANK, BOMBAY -> Aruna Asaf Ali hoists the Congress flag
UNDERGROUND -> Usha Mehta's Congress Radio
UNDERGROUND -> Jayaprakash Narayan and Ram Manohar Lohia organise resistance.
source_references: Do or Die, Gowalia Tank and the underground resistance

panels.title: Parallel governments, social base and results
ascii_lines: PARALLEL GOVERNMENTS -> Ballia; Jatiya Sarkar (Tamluk); Prati Sarkar (Satara)
BASE -> students, workers, peasants; regionally variable intensity
ALIGNMENTS -> League aloof/opposed; CPI People's War line; Mahasabha/princes distant
RESULTS -> suppressed within months; no solo independence; lasting sentiment shown.
source_references: Parallel national governments: Ballia, Tamluk and Satara
Social base, repression caution and political alignments
Results of Quit India and the 2024 Mains anchor
